text: Ah, the humble candle. A marvel of modern engineering, primarily composed of paraffin wax—a petroleum byproduct that smells faintly of a gas station and nostalgia. It is the ultimate symbol of adult sophistication: a stick of solidified oil that you light to create a "cozy ambiance" while you stare blankly at a wall, contemplating whether you remembered to turn off the stove. It burns down, day by day, mirroring your own spirit as you slowly consume your youth in the flickering glow of impending deadlines. Truly, there is nothing more romantic than watching a block of fat melt into a puddle of regret, illuminating the empty space where your dreams used to be.
